clue.text: Square people like to exercise the mind

definitions.text: Square people like to exercise the mind

parts.words: Square people like to exercise the mind
parts.note: the 'square' is the grid of black and white squares, and the people who like it are solvers giving their brains a workout

explanation.definitionFit: A grid of squares filled by solvers is a mental exercise people enjoy.

clue.text: It pays him to do business, but commenting so is a mistake

definitions.text: It pays him to do business

indicators.note: a mistake garbles the words, so the letters of the preceding phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark about a broker whose fee depends on deals, rebuked as erroneous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' signals that COMMENTING SO IS A is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a broker earns a percentage on each deal he makes, so his pay comes from doing business.

clue.text: Russian river spectacle that's quite disgusting

parts.note: the Ob is a great river of Siberia
a scene is a sight or spectacle

explanation.surface: A display on a river in Russia that turns the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lewd or offensive is utterly repellent to decency.

clue.text: Game unsuitable for women

explanation.surface: A sport that ladies should not play.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is hunted as game, and a men-only party is called this, so women are excluded.

clue.text: Cow which needs some cover -a weatherproof shelter

indicators.note: only some of the letters across these words are used, a run lying within them

explanation.surface: Advice that a cow needs a roof over her head in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' is the verb, to intimidate, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them into submission.

clue.text: Act about certain police when so resolved

indicators.note: the word for an act goes round the police letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a deed is an act
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Police make their move once a matter is settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being firmly determined on something is having made a firm choice.

clue.text: Vessels built by seamen in the United States

indicators.note: the sailors are placed inside the country's letters

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States
RN is the Royal Navy, the seamen of Britain

explanation.surface: Ships built by sailors in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships; here they are pots or vases.
explanation.definitionFit: Large vases or containers are vessels.

clue.text: Quickly moving beasts collected valuable pottery

parts.note: a zoo is a collection of animals
Ming porcelain from the Chinese dynasty is famously valuable

explanation.surface: Animals rushing about knocking over precious vases.
explanation.definitionFit: To move at great speed is to rush along fast.

clue.text: Get angry as docilely arranged reduction of shopping facilities

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper over things being placidly ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges ANGRY AS DOCILELY. An early closing day was the weekday when British shops shut at lunchtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops closing at midday on one weekday cut the hours available for shopping.

clue.text: A university man's shrewd where there's friction

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a university graduate, and the 's adds S
sage means wise or shrewd

explanation.surface: A clever graduate in a place of conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friction' suggests disagreement; here it is rubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading and rubbing the body involves friction on the skin.

clue.text: Outline read before a journey

parts.note: to con is to study or read carefully
a tour is a journey

explanation.surface: Studying the plan before setting off on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A line on a map tracing a shape is its outline.

clue.text: Some could hide an elephant, it's thought

indicators.note: only some of the letters across these words are taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: An image of people trying to conceal an elephant, which seems far-fetched.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a thought.

clue.text: Enduring writer

explanation.surface: An author whose work lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough and resilient things endure; Thomas Hardy was the novelist of Wessex.

clue.text: Not straight about one? That's tough!

indicators.note: the crooked word goes round the numeral, surrounding it

parts.note: wry means twisted or not straight
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something bent that proves hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean and sinewy people are tough and resilient.

clue.text: Unhappy about the French food

indicators.note: the sad word goes round the French article, enclosing it

parts.note: sad means unhappy
la is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A complaint about French cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of leaves and vegetables is food.

clue.text: The record of the year

parts.note: reads like a hit single award, but means a chronicle covering a single year's events

explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle entry is a historical record covering one year.

clue.text: Watch attendant find the leak

parts.note: to watch is to see
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: An order to watch a servant locating where water gets in.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid slowly escaping through a gap is a leak.

clue.text: Exceptionally lean dog trained in Ireland

definitions.note: a county in Ireland, so the phrase defines a place there

indicators.note: a dog that is trained is shaped into new behaviour, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An extremely thin hound being trained in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' rearranges LEAN DOG; 'Exceptionally' adds to the surface. Donegal is a county in the far north-west of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This county lies in the north-west of the island, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Working round for a social worker

parts.note: O is round in shape
per means 'for each' or 'for a', as in per day
an ant is a social insect, a worker in a colony

explanation.surface: Doing a round of visits for a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a profession; it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something functioning or in operation is working.

clue.text: Repeated hesitation to hold a traitor-it's not right!

indicators.note: the hesitation sounds grip the traitor word between them

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation
um is a second hesitation sound, so the hesitation is repeated
a rat is a traitor or deserter

explanation.surface: Stammering when confronting a turncoat is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A printing error is something wrongly given, a mistake.

clue.text: Can change course, that's the point

parts.note: a tin is a can
to tack is to change course in sailing

explanation.surface: A remark that being able to alter direction is the whole purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A short nail is a sharp point.

clue.text: A large number of girls in ranks

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, a large number
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Many girls lined up in rows.
explanation.definitionFit: Social grades or categories are ranks.

clue.text: A drawing of a box containing duck

indicators.note: the box word goes round the duck letter

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard box
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A sketch of a box with a duck inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic sketch is a kind of drawing.

clue.text: The arts broadcast causes fragmentation

definitions.note: a verb phrase, matching the verb's sense 'break into pieces'

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Arts programmes on air split the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To smash something into pieces is to break it apart.

clue.text: Battle account given by some soldiers

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops giving a report of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Acre in Palestine was besieged in the Crusades, hence a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The siege of this crusader port was a famous battle.

clue.text: The virtuous man holds no right to express indignation

indicators.note: the saint's letters hold the others inside

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a virtuous man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A good man declining an injustice with an angry noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud nasal snort is a way of showing scorn or outrage.

clue.text: Green cotton

explanation.surface: Describing a fabric's colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassed area is a green; a fine sheer linen or cotton fabric shares the name.

clue.text: Opposing the National Trust in really good environment

indicators.note: the trust's letters go inside those meaning excellent

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: Objecting to the heritage charity in a fine setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something is being opposed to it.

clue.text: Intelligence-given his head's together

parts.note: wit means intelligence

indicators.note: a word's head is its first letter, so only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Clever with his head on straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in company along with someone means being together.

clue.text: The country is at one-unusually!

indicators.note: unusually means arranged in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nation unusually at peace.
explanation.definitionFit: This Baltic state is a country.

clue.text: A doctor returned the object Edward dropped

indicators.note: returned means read backwards, so the doctor letters are turned round

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
it is the object pronoun
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A medic brought back something Edward let fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns MO round to give OM.
explanation.definitionFit: Being left out is being dropped from a list.

clue.text: The general public

parts.note: ordinary people at large, named by three common first names

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of three common first names stands for just anyone, the ordinary people.
